chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimy, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who gives charity from jointly owned property, he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible.'

key_terms.الصَّدَقَةِ: Charity, voluntary alms given for God's sake

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to give charity from jointly owned property in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi through the chain of Zurarah, a primary narrator of Imam al-Baqir (AS), this hadith clarifies the permissibility of donating jointly owned property, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that an owner may dispose of their specific share unless otherwise restricted. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic endowments (waqf) and charity (sadaqah), allowing for partial ownership to be dedicated to charitable causes without invalidating the joint nature of the asset. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the legal mechanics of shared assets in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Asimy, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Muhammad Bin Humran, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the man who gives charity with something which is a jointly owned. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allowed’.
en.sarwar: 26. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from al-‘Asemiy from Ali ibn al-Hassan from Ali ibn Asbat from Muhammad ibn Humran from Zurarah
who has narrated the following: “About the case of a man who gives in charity what is owned in partnership, abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, has said, ‘It is permissible.’”
